title: What Stratospheric Platform Stations Is
definition: Stratospheric Platform Stations: permanent stations floating in the stratosphere.
description:
Stratospheric Platform Stations: permanent stations floating in the stratosphere. This is Future Transport & Mobility at its most ambitious — balloon platforms research, station logistics engineering and position holding operations converging on a single goal: making station hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Transport & Mobility will decide payload bays outcomes this century. Stratospheric Platform Stations is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working station hulls, the larger balloon platforms vision stalls, and with it, the station logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Stratospheric Platform Stations in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Stratospheric Platform Stations
title: Real Research Today: Stratospheric Platform Stations
definition: Today's documented research behind Stratospheric Platform Stations.
description:
The road to Stratospheric Platform Stations is already being paved. Hydrogen aviation programs (Airbus ZEROe, Universal Hydrogen) fly fuel-cell regional aircraft. Autonomous shipping trials (Yara Birkeland, MAS) test crewless cargo vessels.

Stratospheric balloons and airships (Sceye, Flying Whales) return as cargo platforms. Together these programs form the balloon platforms foundation that Stratospheric Platform Stations will build on — the station logistics results, the position holding methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as station logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

definition: 2032 milestone on the Stratospheric Platform Stations roadmap.

First certified station hulls service opens: balloon platforms propulsion carrying paying passengers on station logistics guideways.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed balloon platforms demonstrations, station logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting position holding uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Stratospheric Platform Stations
definition: Estimates Stratospheric Platform Stations readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Stratospheric Platform Stations components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a station hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Stratospheric Platform Stations Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Stratospheric Platform Stations operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Stratospheric Platform Stations installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 82392 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where balloon platforms monitoring, station logistics redundancy, or position holding maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Stratospheric Platform Stations Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Stratospheric Platform Stations: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Stratospheric Platform Stations — permanent stations floating in the stratosphere.

Phase 1 — Prove (balloon platforms): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (station logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (position holding): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (payload bays): station hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and stratosphere-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
